class.name: LocalExposureEffect
class.brief_description: Brings bright and dark parts of the picture towards middle grey, each on its own.
class.description: The eye adapts to bright and dark parts of a scene at once; a camera doesn't. This effect does it for each part of the picture: the light round each pixel is brought towards middle grey, highlights and shadows each by a contrast of their own, so a sunlit sky keeps its clouds while the street below still reads, and a lit sign keeps its lettering at night. The detail within each part is kept, and the scene's exposure (the [Environment]'s and the camera's) still sets the picture's brightness overall. Add it to a [Compositor]'s [member Compositor.compositor_effects], on a [WorldEnvironment] or [Camera3D]. It's drawn after the scene's see-through objects, before tonemapping, with the Forward+ renderer; with the others it draws nothing. In a headset it draws nothing: each eye's picture would be evened out differently.

members.member: How closely it follows edges of brightness: at [code]1[/code], a lit sign beside a dark alley is evened out without darkening the alley; at [code]0[/code], the light round each pixel is a plain blur.
The contrast of the picture's brighter parts against middle grey: below [code]1[/code] they're brought down towards it, above [code]1[/code] pushed further. [code]1[/code] leaves them be.
The contrast of the picture's darker parts against middle grey: below [code]1[/code] they're brought up towards it. [code]1[/code] leaves them be.
